maya: Kicking off a 3h multi-region failover + perf window now. Objective: apples-to-apples comparison between synthetic suites and replay harnesses, focus on kernel selection, batching heuristics, and KV-cache priming/fallback behavior. I'll post replay ids and config shortly.

liam: +1. Which models and regions?

maya: Regions: us-east1 (primary), eu-west1, asia-south1. Models: redwood-13b (default), redwood-7b-fallback (quantized). Synthetic harness will replay uniform prompt mix; replay harness is customer-prod-replay-20260317.

ravi: quick profiler note from initial warmup: high p95 correlated with KV cache misses on eu-west nodes. snippet from node logs:
```
[2026-03-18T15:04:12Z] node-eu-3: model=redwood-13b quant=8bit kernel=matmul-opt seq=256 kv_miss=true p95=420ms p50=120ms
[2026-03-18T15:04:27Z] node-eu-3: kv_prime_start seq=0 prime_tokens=1024
```
Seems like first 60s after a cold start we see lots of kv_miss events.

noa: That's expected. Replay harness doesn't always prime KV prefixes properly. We should enable our priming pass in replay: `--kv-prime 60s` and compare. Also add a synthetic priming run that writes the common prefixes.

aj: I'll add a canary route to flip fallback models on high tail. Command I'm going to run: `./ctl route set --policy fallback --threshold 250ms --fallback-model redwood-7b-fallback --regions eu-west1,asia-south1`

liam: For apples-to-apples, ensure batching heuristics identical between synthetic and replay. Currently synthetic uses dynamic-window=16 and replay uses static-batch=32. That will skew latency. Let's standardize to dynamic-window=20 for this test.

maya: Good catch. Set both harnesses to `batching.mode=dynamic` and `batching.max_window=20`.

ravi: After switching batching we saw baseline improvement: p50 unchanged, p95 improved ~30ms in us-east, but eu-west still high until KV priming completes. Raw numbers from initial 10-min run (synthetic, no priming, dynamic-window=20):
```
us-east1: p50=85ms p95=210ms errors=0.1% qps=220
eu-west1: p50=110ms p95=420ms errors=0.6% qps=180
asia-south1: p50=130ms p95=360ms errors=0.4% qps=140
```

noa: Okay, re-run with replay harness + `--kv-prime 60s`. Also enable kernel-selection logging (`KERNEL_TRACE=1`) so we can correlate p95 spikes with kernel fallback heuristics.

deploy-bot: Canary routing update applied by aj at 15:18 UTC.

ravi: After enabling kv-prime: eu-west p95 dropped to ~200ms after ~45s of traffic. Observed pattern: priming reduces KV miss rate from ~22% to ~3% which directly drops token generation tail. Kernel trace shows initial choice was matmul-opt, then switched to attention-tiling on long sequences when kv_miss spikes occurred.

liam: Interesting — implies kernel selection also depends on cache hit behavior (we expected it to be independent). We should add a test matrix: (kernel-selection forced vs auto) x (kv-prime on/off) x (batching modes).

maya: Agreed. For multi-region failover behavior, aj's fallback policy triggered once for eu-west after we simulated a region CPU pressure spike: route switched to redwood-7b-fallback for ~2m, global latency stayed within SLO but quality delta noticed by eval hooks.

aj: Logs from the failover event: `route-change: eu-west1 -> redwood-7b-fallback at 15:37 due to node pressure threshold=85%` then `route-revert` after pressure normalized. No customer-facing errors.

noa: Action item: add KV priming to our rollout checklist for cold starts and region drains. Also add an automated warmup in the routing controller before flipping live traffic to a drained region.

ravi: Perf regression note: we saw a small regression in throughput on one kernel update — p95 went +40ms in some configs. Kernel team suspects a micro-optim that increased memory pressure and reduced effective batching. Need a repro with profiler: `perf top` + `pagemap` traces.

liam: I'll coordinate an apples-to-apples regression run: same model binary, same kernel commit hash, run synthetic and replay back-to-back, store artifacts. Use `repro-id=apples-20260318-01`.

maya: Summary / next steps: 
- Put KV priming (60s) into replay harness and rollout checklist.
- Standardize batching to dynamic-window=20 for these tests.
- Run kernel-selection matrix (forced vs auto) and capture KERNEL_TRACE.
- Add a short warmup window before shifting traffic during region drains.
- Reproduce kernel perf regression and revert or patch.

liam: I'll own the regression repro. ravi/noa can own KV priming and warmup integration. aj will own routing policy changes. maya will coordinate results and publish a short runbook.

sre-bot: Reminder: scheduled 3h window (multi-region perf) started at 15:15 UTC and will end at 18:15 UTC.

maya: Thanks all. Will post artifacts (replay ids, csvs, flamegraphs) in this thread when available. :rocket:
